source_text: Incutiat adhuc scorpius, homicidam Deum ventilans: horrebo plane spurcum blasphemiae statum de haeretico ore foetentem; sed et talem Deum de fiducia rationis amplectar, qua ratione etiam ipse se plus quam homicidam pronuntiavit ex Sophiae suae persona, voce Salomonis: Sophia, inquit, jugulavit filios suos. Sophia, sapientia est. Sapienter utique jugulavit, dum in vitam; et rationaliter, dum in gloriam. O parricidii ingenium! o sceleris artificium! o argumentum crudelitatis, quae idcirco occidit, ne moriatur quem occiderit! Et ideo quid sequitur? Sophia in exitibus cantatur hymnis,; cantatur enim et exitus martyrum. Sophia in plateis de constantia agit, bene enim filios suos jugulat. Super summos autem muros confisa dicit, cum quidem secundum Isaiam hic exclamat: Ego Dei sum; et hic vociferatur: In nomine Jacob; et alius scribit, In nomine Israelis. O bonam matrem! Opto et ipse in filios ejus redigi, ut ab ea occidar. Opto occidi, ut filius fiam. Solum autem jugulat filios suos; an et torquet? Audio enim et alibi dicentem Deum: Uram illos sicuti uritur argentum, et probabo illos sicuti probatur aurum. Utique per tormenta ignium et suppliciorum, per martyria fidei examinatoria. Scit et Apostolus qualem Deum adscripserit, cum scribit: Si Deus Filio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis tradidit illum, quomodo non et cum illo omnia condonavit nobis? Vides quomodo etiam proprium suum Filium primogenitum et unigenitum Sophia divina jugulaverit; utique victurum, imo et caeteros in vitam redacturum. Possum dicere cum Sophia Dei: Christus est qui se tradidit pro delictis nostris. Jam et semetipsam Sophia trucidavit. Verba non sono solo sapiunt, sed et sensu: nec auribus tantummodo audienda sunt, sed et mentibus. Crudelem Deum, qui non intelligit, credit. Quamquam et non intelligenti posita sententia est, quae temeritatem cohibeat aliter intelligendi. Quis enim, inquit, cognovit sensum Dei? aut quis illi consiliarius fuit, qui eum instruat? aut viam intelligentiae quis demonstravit illi? Sed enim Scytharum Dianam, aut Gallorum Mercurium, aut Afrorum Saturnum, hominum victima placari apud saeculum licuit. Et Latio ad hodiernum Jovi media in urbe humanus sanguis ingustatur; nec quisquam retractat, aut non rationem praesumit aliquam, aut inaestimabilem Dei sui voluntatem. Si noster quoque Deus propriae hostiae nomine martyria sibi depostulasset, quis illi exprobrasset funestam religionem, et lugubres ritus, et aram rogum, et pollinctorem sacerdotem? et non beatum amplius reputasset, quem Deus comedisset?
pass_a_gloss: The scorpion still stings, ventilating God as a murderer; I will certainly shudder at the foul state of blasphemy foetentem from the heretic's mouth; but I will also embrace such a God with confidence in reason, by which reason He Himself also declared Himself to be more than a murderer from the person of His Wisdom, in the voice of Solomon: Wisdom, He says, has slain her sons. Wisdom is intelligence. She has certainly slain wisely, since into life, and rationally, since into glory. Oh, the genius of parricide! Oh, the art of crime! Oh, the argument of cruelty, which kills for this reason, so that the one it kills may not die! And therefore, what follows? Wisdom is sung in hymns at the exits; for the exits of martyrs are also sung. Wisdom acts with constancy in the streets, for she slays her sons well. But on the highest walls, trusting, she says, since indeed according to Isaiah she exclaims here: I am of God; and here she cries out: In the name of Jacob; and another writes: In the name of Israel. Oh, good mother! I also wish to be reduced to her sons, so that I may be killed by her. I wish to be killed, so that I may become a son. Does she only slay her sons, or also torment them? For I hear God saying elsewhere: I will refine them like silver is refined, and I will test them like gold is tested. Certainly, through the torments of fire and punishments, through the martyrdoms that test faith. The Apostle also knows what kind of God he has ascribed, when he writes: If God did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us, how will He not also give us all things with Him? You see how even His own firstborn and only-begotten Son, divine Wisdom has slain; certainly, so that He may live, and also lead others back into life. I can say with the Wisdom of God: Christ is the one who handed Himself over for our sins. Now Wisdom has also slaughtered herself. Words do not only sound, but also have meaning; nor are they to be heard only with the ears, but also with the minds. The one who does not understand believes in a cruel God. Although a sentence has also been set for the one who does not understand, which restrains the temerity of understanding otherwise. For who, He says, has known the mind of God? Or who has been His counselor, to instruct Him? Or who has shown Him the way of intelligence? But indeed, it was permitted to placate the Diana of the Scythians, or the Mercury of the Gauls, or the Saturn of the Africans, with human victims in the world; and in Latium, human blood is still poured out to Jupiter in the middle of the city; nor does anyone retract, or does not presume some reason, or the incomprehensible will of their god. If our God had also demanded martyrdoms for Himself in the name of His own victim, who would have reproached Him for a funereal religion, and mournful rites, and a funeral pyre for an altar, and a polluting priest? And would He not have been considered blessed anymore, whom God had devoured?

bible_refs.note: If God did not spare His own Son

pass_b_english: The scorpion still stings, branding God a murderer; I certainly shudder at the foul blasphemy reeking from a heretic's mouth. Yet I embrace such a God with the confidence of reason, the very reason by which He declared Himself more than a murderer through the person of His Wisdom, speaking in Solomon's voice: "Wisdom has slain her sons" (Proverbs 8:36). Wisdom is intelligence; she has certainly slain wisely, since it leads to life, and rationally, since it leads to glory. Oh, the genius of parricide! Oh, the art of crime! Oh, the argument of cruelty that kills precisely so the one killed may not die! What follows? Wisdom is sung in hymns at the exits, for the exits of martyrs are also sung. Wisdom acts with constancy in the streets, for she slays her sons well. Trusting on the highest walls, she speaks: according to Isaiah she exclaims here, "I am of God" (Isaiah 44:24), here she cries, "In the name of Jacob," and another writes, "In the name of Israel." Oh, good mother! I wish to be reckoned among her sons so she may kill me; I wish to be killed so I may become a son. Does she only slay her sons, or also torment them? For I hear God saying elsewhere: "I will refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested." Certainly through the torments of fire and punishments, through martyrdoms that test faith. The Apostle knows the kind of God he ascribes when he writes: "If God did not spare His own Son but handed Him over for us, how will He not also with Him graciously give us all things?" (Romans 8:32). You see how divine Wisdom has slain even His own firstborn and only-begotten Son — certainly so that He may live, and lead others back to life. I can say with the Wisdom of God: Christ is the one who handed Himself over for our sins. Now Wisdom has also slaughtered herself. Words do not merely sound; they have meaning. They are not to be heard only with ears, but with minds. The one who does not understand believes in a cruel God. Yet a sentence has been set for the one who does not understand, restraining the temerity of understanding otherwise: "Who has known the mind of God? Or who has been His counselor to instruct Him? Or who has shown Him the way of understanding?" But indeed, it was permitted in the world to placate the Diana of the Scythians, or the Mercury of the Gauls, or the Saturn of the Africans, with human victims; and in Latium to this day human blood is poured out to Jupiter in the middle of the city. No one retracts, or presumes some reason, or the incomprehensible will of their god. If our God had also demanded martyrdoms for Himself in the name of His own victim, who would have reproached Him for a funereal religion, mournful rites, a funeral pyre for an altar, a polluting priest? And would he not be considered blessed, whom God had devoured?
